title: Comet Lemmon: brighter at the colour of carbon dioxide
claim: On 25 and 26 February 2026 the brightest photo of comet C/2025 A6 (Lemmon) inside the carbon-dioxide band (4.20 to 4.32 µm) was at least 5 times brighter than the photos taken at the nearest colours on either side of the band.
test: Detector 5 photographed the comet 16 times on the two nights, each time at another colour; 15 photos could be measured (a photo with too many flagged pixels in the aperture gives no flux). Flux in an aperture of 2 pixels (12.3 arcsec) radius at the position JPL Horizons gives for the comet seen from SPHEREx; background from a ring of 40 to 55 pixels. The fluxes are lower limits, because the comet's glow reaches the ring: round the comet at 4.266 µm the sky level falls from 0.70 MJy/sr at 15 to 25 pixels to 0.44 in the ring and 0.41 just beyond it, while at the same place in August 2025 it is level (0.35, 0.34 and 0.34). Contrast of a night = the brightest photo of that night inside the band, over the mean of the two photos nearest the band: 4.193 µm (26 February) below it and 4.384 µm (25 February) above it, so each night takes one neighbour from the other night. The error counts the noise of the pixels, the background, and the scatter of up to 20 empty apertures of the same colour in each photo. Checks: with a ring of 15 to 25 pixels the contrast is 16.7 and 10.2; with an aperture of 5 pixels 10.9 and 8.5; with every aperture shifted by up to 0.2 pixel it stays between 12.7 and 17.3, and between 9.0 and 11.3. With any one photo left out that is not a night's brightest, the lowest contrast is 6.7. With a night's brightest photo left out, the next brightest gives: 25 February 3.1; 26 February 8.1; on 25 February the other photo inside the band sits at its edge, so that night's figure rests on a single photo. In the photo at 4.119 µm a star of the Gaia catalogue (G magnitude 12.8) lies 1.5 pixels from the comet and adds to its flux; that photo is not one of the three used.
pass_rule: The contrast is 5 or more on both nights.
plain: brighter at the colour of carbon dioxide on both nights

title: Comet Lemmon: the same sky without the comet
claim: For each of the 5 photos of the comet taken inside the band, a photo of August 2025 at the same colour shows nothing at the comet's place: the brightness belongs to the comet, not to that patch of sky.
test: For each of the 5 photos inside the band, the August 2025 photos of detector 5 that hold the same place were matched against it by the site's match rule (same detector, closest colour at that place, within half a bandwidth); the chosen templates differ in colour by 1.4 to 12.4 nm. Same aperture (2 pixels) and ring (40 to 55 pixels) at the same sky position. Template fluxes: -0.1, +1.5, +0.3, +0.5, +0.7 mJy against 162.5, 52.7, 136.2, 263.2, 71.7 mJy for the comet. Standard errors include the scatter of empty apertures of the same colour in both photos, which in this crowded field is far larger than the noise of the pixels (with the noise of the pixels and of the background alone, the smallest excess is 112 standard errors). The comet's two brightest positions are 52.2 arcmin and 37.5 hours apart, and the centre of its light lies 0.4 and 0.2 pixels from the JPL Horizons position.
pass_rule: Every template flux is under 5% of the comet's flux at that place, and every photo inside the band other than a night's brightest exceeds its template by 5 standard errors or more.
plain: nothing there in August 2025 at the same colour
value: largest template 2.9% of its comet flux; smallest excess 5.3 standard errors

title: Comet Lemmon: an earlier figure, corrected
claim: An earlier version of this analysis said the comet's excess inside the band was 88 times the scatter of empty sky. Measured on enough empty sky it is 4.7 times.
test: The earlier figure divided the excess by the scatter of the same estimate on 8 tracks of empty apertures, which happened to miss the stars of the field. On 128 empty tracks, some of which cross stars, the scatter is larger and the same excess is 4.7 times it. Both figures were measured on 14 November 2026 with an earlier estimate of the excess; this job does not compute them again, and the site quotes neither: it quotes the contrast of row K2.
pass_rule: Not a pass or fail test: a correction kept on record.
unit: times the scatter of empty tracks
